roots.name: What is terminal velocity? - Physics Daily
roots.value: Terminal velocity is the constant speed a falling object reaches when air resistance balances its weight. The object stops accelerating at that point.

roots.name: What is terminal velocity? - Physics Daily
roots.value: A belly-down skydiver reaches a terminal velocity of about 55 m/s (200 km/h). Pulling into a head-down position can raise that to roughly 90 m/s.

roots.name: What is terminal velocity? - Physics Daily
roots.value: A small steel ball has a much higher terminal velocity than a feather because its weight is large compared with the drag it experiences.

roots.name: What is terminal velocity? - Physics Daily
roots.value: Drag depends on the cross-sectional area facing the air and on a drag coefficient that captures how streamlined the body is. A flat, spread-out body presents a large area and falls slowly; a narrow, pointed body falls much faster.

ancestor_path.name: What is terminal velocity? - Physics Daily

roots.name: What is terminal velocity? - Physics Daily
roots.value: Air density also changes the answer. In thinner air at high altitude the same body falls faster, which is why a jump from very high up begins with extreme speeds before the atmosphere thickens.
